instructions: Put 6 cups of water on to boil in a kettle or a pot.
Rinse the split peas in a strainer until the water runs clear. Finely dice the onion and carrots, mince the garlic, and pick the leaves from the thyme.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and garlic. Cook, stirring, for 3 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Add the split peas, the bay leaves, the thyme leaves, 1 tsp of the salt and the boiling water. Bring it back to a boil, skim off any foam with a spoon, then cover and turn the heat to medium-low.
Simmer for 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas fall apart when you press one against the side of the pot. If they're still firm, give them 5 minutes longer.
While the peas simmer, finely dice half of the red onion. Slice the tomatoes and cucumber, and chop 1/4 cup of the parsley. Drain the capers.
Take the pot off the heat and remove the bay leaves. Juice the lemons. That should be about 1/3 cup.

Add the lemon juice and 1/4 cup of the oil, then blend with an immersion blender until it's smooth and creamy. If it's too thick, stir in a splash of hot water. If it's too thin, simmer it for 2 minutes, stirring.
Season with the remaining 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the fava into shallow bowls. Top with the diced red onion, capers and parsley, and drizzle with the remaining 2 tbsp oil.
Serve with the sliced tomatoes, cucumber and olives.
method_notes: Both sources simmer yellow split peas with onion and garlic until they fall apart, then blend them with lemon juice and olive oil. The lead sautés red onion and thyme first and simmers 40 to 50 minutes. The other adds carrot and bay leaves and simmers about 45 minutes. This version sautés the vegetables only 3 minutes and starts with boiling water so the peas are soft in 28 minutes. That puts the total at exactly 45 minutes with no slack, so an older bag of peas may need 5 more. Capers, parsley and red onion are the topping, and sliced tomato, cucumber and olives make it a meal. It is vegan and gluten-free as written.
